Messages.Author: Athenethor
Messages.Body:
Hi,

I have on question for the group. What will happens to the next situation:

Acting vampire A is blocking by vampire B. In the strike declaration, minion
A play a Majesty, and minion B play a wolf claws. As the minion B is blockin
and is trying to inflict agravated damage, I suppose he can play a
Rotschreck to send minion A to torpor.

How is resolved the above combat?

Another question is: When takes effect the strike: combat ends? In the
strike resolution or as the card (Majesty for example) is played?

Thanks

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Wed, 26 Apr 2000, Athenethor wrote:
> Acting vampire A is blocking by vampire B. In the strike declaration, minion
> A play a Majesty, and minion B play a wolf claws. As the minion B is blockin
> and is trying to inflict agravated damage, I suppose he can play a
> Rotschreck to send minion A to torpor.
>
> How is resolved the above combat?

The Methuselah controlling minion B plays Rotschreck. Combat
ends. Minion A goes to torpor, as per Rotschreck text.

> Another question is: When takes effect the strike: combat ends? In the
> strike resolution or as the card (Majesty for example) is played?

The first item of strike resolution.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Athenethor wrote:
> Acting vampire A is blocking by vampire B. In the strike declaration, minion
> A play a Majesty, and minion B play a wolf claws.

Meaning that minion B declares "hands" as his strike and also (before
moving to the strike resolution step) plays Wolf Claws.

> As the minion B is blockin
> and is trying to inflict agravated damage, I suppose he can play a
> Rotschreck to send minion A to torpor.

Yes. (Actually, minions don't play Master cards - so technically, minion
B's controller would play Rotschreck)

Note: "Blocking" isn't required - the only thing that is important is
that it isn't minion B's controller's turn.

> How is resolved the above combat?

Minion B's controlled plays Rotschreck (before strike resolution).
Combat immediately ends.
Vampire A goes to torpor.

> Another question is: When takes effect the strike: combat ends? In the
> strike resolution or as the card (Majesty for example) is played?

When Strike Resolution begins.
(or "would begin", however you prefer to say it)
